methodology: Expanding, selected, attributed incident and regional report catalogue affecting Assyrian people and historically linked Syriac and other Christian church communities. Entries may cover distinct single events, town-level episodes, or broad campaigns, with overlapping episodes sometimes cross-referenced in their descriptions. Source evidence ranges from scholarly history and formal human-rights reports to attributed community accounts. A reported allegation is not presented as a proven finding. The heat map represents the number of catalogue entries, not victims, severity, persecution rates, or unique campaigns. Country inclusion follows the recorded location of an event, not the residence of witnesses or exiles. Place coordinates are approximate and may identify only the town or region. Unrepresented countries do not imply absence of persecution.

records.title: Wakeley Assyrian church stabbing of bishop and priest
records.summary: An assailant stabbed Bishop Mar Mari Emmanuel and injured a priest during a live-streamed service at an Assyrian Orthodox church in western Sydney. Police classified the event as religiously motivated terrorism; legal and mental-health proceedings continued later, so this report does not assert a final verdict.
records.actor: 16-year-old male defendant, with charges and motive subject to judicial proceedings

records.title: Reported vandalism at Assyrian Chaldean Catholic church in Antwerp
records.summary: An Assyrian community publication reported a symbol spray-painted on the door of a church serving Assyrian Chaldean Catholics in Antwerp. The incident had not been independently established by official Belgian reporting when the account was published.
records.actor: Unidentified vandal; motive and police outcome unconfirmed

sources.title: Reported vandalism at Assyrian church in Antwerp - The Assyria Post (2026)

records.title: Syriac Orthodox monastery property transferred to state bodies
records.summary: Following administrative reorganisation, multiple Syriac Orthodox church and monastery properties were transferred into Turkish public control, prompting opposition. A 2018 decree ordered restitution of 30 assets, which must be recorded to avoid implying permanent seizure.
records.actor: Turkish public authorities; later restitution ordered

sources.title: Restitution decree for Syriac Orthodox properties - Agenzia Fides (2018)

records.title: Disappearance of Assyrian Christian couple Hurmuz and Simoni Diril
records.summary: Two elderly Assyrian-linked Chaldean Catholic villagers disappeared from their home. Simoni's body was found in March 2020; her husband's fate remained unresolved at the time of the cited report. Claims about the abductors were allegations, not established findings.
records.actor: Unknown kidnappers; affiliation allegations contested or unproven

records.place: St Mary of the Holy Belt Cathedral, Homs
records.title: Shots fired at Syriac Orthodox cathedral cross in Homs
records.summary: The Syriac Orthodox Archdiocese of Homs, Hama and Tartus reported gunfire directed at a cross on the facade of its Cathedral of St Mary of the Holy Belt in the Bustan al-Diwan quarter. Clergy denounced intimidation, and the perpetrators were not identified in the report.
